Here is the recipe JSON:
{
  "recipe_name": "Vegetarian Pizza",
  "ingredients": [
    "1 1/2 cups warm water",
    "2 teaspoons sugar",
    "2 teaspoons active dry yeast",
    "3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour",
    "1 teaspoon salt",
    "1/4 cup olive oil",
    "1/2 cup pizza sauce",
    "1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese",
    "1 cup shredded ricotta cheese",
    "1 cup sliced bell peppers",
    "1 cup sliced onions",
    "1 cup sliced mushrooms",
    "1 cup sliced tomatoes",
    "Fresh basil leaves"
  ],
  "steps": [
    {
      "step_number": 1,
      "instruction": "In a large mixing bowl, combine warm water, sugar, and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until yeast is activated.",
      "time": "10 minutes",
      "tip": "Make sure the water is not too hot, as it can kill the yeast."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 2,
      "instruction": "Add flour, salt, and olive oil to the bowl. Mix until a dough forms.",
      "time": "5 minutes",
      "tip": "Use a stand mixer with a dough hook attachment for easier mixing."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 3,
      "instruction": "Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.",
      "time": "10 minutes",
      "tip": "You can also knead the dough by hand if you don't have a stand mixer."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 4,
      "instruction": "Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours until it doubles in size.",
      "time": "1-2 hours",
      "tip": "Make sure the bowl is large enough to hold the dough as it rises."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 5,
      "instruction": "Preheat the oven to 425\u00b0F (220\u00b0C). Punch down the dough and roll it out into a circle or rectangle shape.",
      "time": "5 minutes",
      "tip": "Use a pizza stone or baking sheet to bake the pizza."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 6,
      "instruction": "Spread pizza sauce over the dough, leaving a small border around the edges.",
      "time": "2 minutes",
      "tip": "You can use homemade or store-bought pizza sauce."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 7,
      "instruction": "Top the pizza with mozzarella cheese, ricotta cheese, bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, and tomatoes.",
      "time": "5 minutes",
      "tip": "Feel free to customize the toppings to your liking."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 8,
      "instruction": "Bake the pizza in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly.",
      "time": "15-20 minutes",
      "tip": "Keep an eye on the pizza to avoid overcooking."
    },
    {
      "step_number": 9,
      "instruction": "Remove the pizza from the oven and sprinkle with fresh basil leaves.",
      "time": "1 minute",
      "tip": "Let the pizza cool for a few minutes before slicing and serving."
    }
  ]
}
i want to make with atta

You want to make a pizza using atta (whole wheat flour) instead of all-purpose flour. That's a great idea. To make an atta pizza, you can follow the same steps as before, but keep in mind that atta can be a bit more dense and heavier than all-purpose flour.

When using atta, you may need to adjust the water content and the kneading time. Atta typically requires more water than all-purpose flour, so you can start with the same amount of water and add more as needed to get the right consistency.

Also, atta can be a bit more difficult to knead, so you may need to knead it for a longer time to get the dough smooth and elastic.
